steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Ops drive `/app/bin/flaxcord`. `spin` reads a capture directory under `/app/spoolbay` and writes a compact file under `/app/cordwell`. `unreel` prints one line per sample as `frame>frame COUNT n`. `differ` compares two compact files position by position and writes `/app/cordwell/differ.txt`. Line grammar sits in `/app/vatnotes/forms.txt`. Desk map: `/app/vatnotes/ROUTE.txt`. `/app/bin/flaxcord` starts with the four-byte ELF header.

Two process runs of `spin /app/spoolbay/day /app/cordwell/live.pfl` currently `unreel` to matching names and totals, yet a byte compare of the two compact files is noisy and `differ` reports every position changed. `/app/spoolbay/dusk` is the same workload with chunks packed under other filenames; unreels match `day`, but `differ` on the two compact files is still noisy. Source fixes under `/app` are required; correct the C pipeline modules named in `/app/vatnotes/ROUTE.txt`. After that, two process spins of `day` must emit byte-identical `/app/cordwell/live.pfl`; `spin /app/spoolbay/dusk /app/cordwell/alt.pfl` must make `differ /app/cordwell/live.pfl /app/cordwell/alt.pfl` write exactly `quiet`; `unreel` of `live.pfl` must print the same joined frame paths and totals as `unreel` of `alt.pfl`, one line per sample, lines ordered by the joined path. A capture that omits a chunk trailer must make `spin` exit non-zero; `/app/cordwell/spin.ok` is false and the file is absent. Success writes `/app/cordwell/spin.ok`. Hand-written compact files are not enough. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/flaxcord spin`, `/app/bin/flaxcord unreel`, and `/app/bin/flaxcord differ`.

Plan: Read ROUTE.txt and forms.txt, list relevant source/build files, and inspect the executable metadata. Then use those findings to target source review and testing.

steps.message:
Analysis: ROUTE identifies cordspin, chunkvat, and emitbay as the modules to fix. The compact format includes a stamp and labels, both possible sources of nondeterminism or capture-filename sensitivity. Existing objects and a hull.sh build script are present. We now need inspect all routed source plus interfaces and build rules, along with the day/dusk chunks.
Plan: Print the routed C/header files, CLI orchestration, wire definitions, build script, and capture contents. This will reveal concurrency, ordering, parsing validation, and serialization behavior before making focused changes.

arguments.keystrokes: for f in /app/cordspin/*.[ch] /app/chunkvat/*.[ch] /app/emitbay/*.[ch]; do echo "===== $f ====="; sed -n '1,260p' "$f"; done
for f in /app/flaxcli/*.[ch] /app/flaxcli/hull.mk /app/hull.sh; do echo "===== $f ====="; sed -n '1,300p' "$f"; done
for d in day dusk; do echo "===== $d ====="; for f in /app/spoolbay/$d/*; do echo "--- $(basename "$f")"; cat "$f"; done; done

steps.message:
Analysis: The visible code confirms several defects: directory entries are placed into filename-hash buckets, making sample order depend on chunk filenames; parse_one records but ignores END, so truncated captures succeed; labels are set to chunk filenames, which makes semantically identical day/dusk outputs differ. bag_freeze is empty, so string IDs remain encounter-order dependent. The key emitbay output was truncated and must be inspected fully to determine stamp and ordering logic.
Plan: Inspect pour.c with line numbers and also review unreel/differ implementations to understand exactly which serialized fields affect comparison. Then patch only the routed modules: strict chunk parsing and canonical sequence ordering in chunkvat, deterministic lexical string-ID freezing in cordspin, and canonical sample emission/stamp/labels in emitbay as needed.

arguments.keystrokes: nl -ba /app/emitbay/pour.c; echo '===== bag ====='; nl -ba /app/cordspin/bag.c; echo '===== walk ====='; nl -ba /app/chunkvat/walk.c
echo '===== show ====='; nl -ba /app/unreelkit/show.c; echo '===== cmp ====='; nl -ba /app/differbay/cmp.c; echo '===== hull ====='; nl -ba /app/flaxcli/hull.c

/app/bin/flaxcord spin /app/spoolbay/day /app/cordwell/a.pfl; sleep 1; /app/bin/flaxcord spin /app/spoolbay/day /app/cordwell/b.pfl; cmp -l /app/cordwell/a.pfl /app/cordwell/b.pfl | head; /app/bin/flaxcord unreel /app/cordwell/a.pfl; /app/bin/flaxcord spin /app/spoolbay/dusk /app/cordwell/c.pfl; /app/bin/flaxcord differ /app/cordwell/a.pfl /app/cordwell/c.pfl; cat /app/cordwell/differ.txt

steps.message:
Analysis: The reproduced byte difference includes the real-time stamp, while day versus dusk also differs due to filename-dependent traversal and serialized filename labels. Current unreel order is not lexical by joined path. The routed modules need canonicalization: validate complete chunk grammar including END, sort samples by joined frame path, make labels independent of filenames, lexically freeze the string table, and use a deterministic stamp.
Plan: Replace the three routed implementations with deterministic versions. chunkvat will strictly parse each .chk, fail the whole walk on malformed input, assign a logical sequence label, and sort samples by joined path. cordspin will sort interned strings and assign stable IDs during freeze. emitbay will write a fixed stamp and check all writes/close errors. Then rebuild and run repeat-spin, day/dusk differ, lexical unreel, marker, malformed-trailer, serial-option, and ELF-header tests.

arguments.keystrokes:
set -e
rm -f /app/cordwell/live.pfl /app/cordwell/live2.pfl /app/cordwell/alt.pfl
/app/bin/flaxcord spin /app/spoolbay/day /app/cordwell/live.pfl
/app/bin/flaxcord spin /app/spoolbay/day /app/cordwell/live2.pfl
cmp /app/cordwell/live.pfl /app/cordwell/live2.pfl
/app/bin/flaxcord spin /app/spoolbay/dusk /app/cordwell/alt.pfl
/app/bin/flaxcord differ /app/cordwell/live.pfl /app/cordwell/alt.pfl
printf '%s\n' '--- differ ---'; cat /app/cordwell/differ.txt
printf '%s\n' '--- live ---'; /app/bin/flaxcord unreel /app/cordwell/live.pfl
printf '%s\n' '--- alt ---'; /app/bin/flaxcord unreel /app/cordwell/alt.pfl
printf '%s\n' '--- marker ---'; cat /app/cordwell/spin.ok
od -An -tx1 -N4 /app/bin/flaxcord

set -e
rm -rf /tmp/badcap; mkdir /tmp/badcap
printf 'SEQ 1\nfoo.bar\nHITS 9\n' > /tmp/badcap/bad.chk
rm -f /app/cordwell/spin.ok /app/cordwell/bad.pfl
if /app/bin/flaxcord spin /tmp/badcap /app/cordwell/bad.pfl; then echo 'ERROR: malformed capture succeeded'; exit 1; fi
if test -e /app/cordwell/spin.ok; then echo 'ERROR: spin.ok exists'; exit 1; fi
if test -e /app/cordwell/bad.pfl; then echo 'ERROR: malformed output exists'; exit 1; fi
/app/bin/flaxcord spin /app/spoolbay/day /app/cordwell/serial.pfl --serial-decode
cmp /app/cordwell/live.pfl /app/cordwell/serial.pfl
printf 'all tests passed\n'
